mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong labor market growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and exerts downward pressure on the S&P 500 over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 persons alongside a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points signals a deterioration in labor market quality despite headline job growth, which reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 AND UNRATE > previous month + 0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below -0.3% signals deflationary pressure, prompting expectations of accommodative central bank policy, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 8% signals a tightening in household balance sheets and reduced housing investment, which depresses consumption and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < 0 AND HOUST monthly change < -8%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based acceleration in manufacturing activity, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.4% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).
